source: curated seed list of real official portals/platforms; every entry starts seed_unverified and is upgraded ONLY by deterministic government-domain verification and/or live credential-free recon. Entries that fail verification stay unreleased.
notes: One family per real platform. A family may serve many destinations, nationalities and jurisdictions — adapters are built per family and reused. No entry may be invented; uncertain platforms are omitted (their routes stay honestly unresolved).

entries.name: U.S. ESTA (Electronic System for Travel Authorization)

actions.purpose: Close the 'DOWNLOAD THE ESTA APP' splash modal that opens on every fresh load of https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/. Its .modal-backdrop swallows all clicks until dismissed. TIMING GOTCHA: the modal's vertical position shifts by ~140 CSS px as its two QR-code images finish loading, so wait for network idle / re-measure the element rect immediately before clicking, or click via element handle rather than a cached coordinate. Verified: selector matches exactly 1 element (text 'CLOSE'); after the click #splashModal computed display went 'block' -> 'none' and .modal-backdrop count went 1 -> 0.

'Start New Individual Application' button inside #what-section on the home page (below the fold, ~y=1410 at 1280x900). Verified: unique id, innerText 'START NEW INDIVIDUAL APPLICATION', click navigated the SPA to https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/disclaimer. EQUIVALENT VERIFIED ALTERNATIVE (above the fold, 2 clicks): CLICK '.btn-group:has(> .create-app-dropdown-menu) > button.dropdown-toggle' then CLICK '.create-app-dropdown-menu li:first-child a' (text 'Individual Application').

'CONFIRM & CONTINUE' in the 'SECURITY NOTIFICATION' modal #confirmModal (DHS system-use notice). CONDITIONAL STEP: it is gated on sessionStorage['estaNoticeAccept'] !== 'true', so it appears exactly once per browser session - on the first Apply click of a fresh context. Treat as optional/if-present rather than a hard-fail step. Verified: appeared on my first pass with #confirmModal visible and buttons #cancelBtn / #confirmBtn; clicking #confirmBtn landed on /disclaimer. On my second pass in the same session it was skipped and sessionStorage read back {'estaNoticeAccept':'true'}.

Disclaimer panel, 'Yes, I have read and understand the information and agree to these terms.' (the 'No' option is #optionsRadios2, which opens an info modal). Verified: after the click input.checked === true and the MDL label gained class 'is-checked'. Side effect: this auto-expands the second accordion panel #2collapseTwo ('panel-collapse collapse' -> 'panel-collapse collapse in'), so #travelRadios1 has a zero-size rect until this step runs.

'The Travel Promotion Act of 2009' panel, 'Yes, I have read and understand the information and agree to these terms.' ('No' is #travelRadios2). Verified: after the click input.checked === true and the NEXT button became actionable. Both radios are MDL custom controls with a 0x0 native input - click the wrapping label / element handle, not the input rect.

'NEXT' at the bottom of /disclaimer. Verified: selector matches exactly 1 element on that page with innerText 'NEXT' (the sibling EXIT button is btn-default). Click navigated to https://esta.cbp.dhs.gov/applicantInfo. An invisible reCAPTCHA v3 (textarea[name='g-recaptcha-response']) is armed on this page and passed silently on both of my runs - no visual challenge was presented.

entry_gate.description: Landing page -> scroll to footer -> click the stable 'E-Visa Application' footer link (a.footer-link[href="/visa"]) -> /visa, which is the full application wizard (Visa Category / Arrival Information / Personal Information / Passport Information / Review / Attachments) rendered as a single SPA page. Wizard step 1 (VISA SELECTION) shows a visaType select plus an 'I agree to the terms and conditions' checkbox; the gate deliberately does not tick it (true T&C consent, not an instructions acknowledgment) — visa-type selection and the consent are fill-tier/user actions. All later-step fields (arrivalDate, departureCountry, departureCity, airline, flightNumber, accommodation*, firstName, surname, citizenship, gender, countryOfBirth, dateOfBirth, placeOfBirth, emailAddress, emailAddressConfirmation, phoneNumber, occupation, streetAddress, addressCity, addressCountry, passportType, passportNumber, passportExpireDate, issuingCountry, passportIssuingAuthority) are already present in the /visa page DOM, hidden until their wizard step activates; native inputs are visually masked by custom-styled widgets, so strict is_visible() fails on them — hence the container-based form_ready_selector.

entry_gate.description: Hash-routed Angular SPA (app.travellerdeclaration.govt.nz/#/...), so the form has NO directly-loadable path and MUST be reached by replay. Verified live 2026-08-02: landing #/ -> New declaration -> #/intro -> Start your declaration -> #/privacy -> tick the privacy route-guard flag -> Next -> #/onboarding (4 applicant fields, first is input[name="contactEmail"]). Deep-linking past #/privacy redirects back to #/, so the checkbox step cannot be skipped. Gate replay starts at the family base_url, which must be https://app.travellerdeclaration.govt.nz/ (the landing route).

actions.purpose: 'New declaration' on the landing page: leaves #/ for the declaration intro. The landing page has 3 buttons (New declaration, Edit declaration, Select language); Edit declaration is mat-button not mat-flat-button and Select language is color=link, so this selector resolves to exactly 1 element. No id, data-testid or formcontrolname exists on this control. Allow ~900ms of SPA routing after the click.

'Start your declaration': advances #/intro -> #/privacy. Stable name attribute. Do NOT use the sibling button[name="completeOnBehalfOf"] ('Start a declaration for someone else', href #/privacy-onbehalf) which forks into a different route family. Allow ~900ms of SPA routing after the click.

Privacy acknowledgment on #/privacy: 'I have read and understood the privacy policy, and understand how my personal information is being collected and used.' Mandatory client-side route-guard flag - Next stays disabled until it is ticked and deep-linking past #/privacy bounces to #/. Verified purely client-side: resource count 88 before and 88 after, zero network requests, no record created. Angular Material MDC checkbox: the id is the auto-generated mat-mdc-checkbox-0-input, so match on the stable name; check the native input so Angular change detection fires (its painted label is label[for="mat-mdc-checkbox-0-input"], usable as a fallback if the native control ever reports 0x0).

'Next': advances #/privacy -> #/onboarding, the first real applicant form. On #/privacy this selector resolves to exactly 1 element. It is disabled until the previous CHECK lands, so a failure here means the checkbox did not take.

entry_gate.description: The form URL /en/create IS directly loadable (curated as a form_path so recon can observe it), but it renders only the traveller-type chooser until two SegmentedControl answers are given - the real applicant fields (Airline, Flight Number, Country of Departure, Port of Departure, Intended Date of Arrival) appear only after Non-Citizen + Air. The gate therefore replays the whole path from the family base_url https://travel.gov.tt/ (landing -> modal -> /en/create -> Non-Citizen -> Air) so the observed artifact contains real fields. Steps 1-2 are the modal route and are skippable for anyone starting at /en/create; they are included because the gate replay always starts at base_url. Mantine SegmentedControl needs a REAL pointer event (Playwright locator.click), never a synthetic element.click() or a blind coordinate press.

Clearing stage 2 dismisses #emailVerify and the backdrop and releases form#cfiveForm. ORDERING CAVEAT for the generated flow: this OTP is an ENTRY gate, so the applicant handoff must be satisfied BEFORE any fill step, not at review/submit where captcha/otp handoffs are placed by default.
